title: Export (OBJ, PLY, STL, Asset), import, materials

sections.heading: EXPORT FORMATS
sections.content:
ProBuilder provides an extensible model export pipeline orchestrated by the `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.Export` action (`MenuAction`), located in `ToolbarGroup.Object` with icon `Toolbar/Object_Export`. The exporter supports five discrete target formats defined by the `Export.ExportFormat` enum: `Obj`, `Stl`, `Ply`, `Asset`, and `Prefab`.

1. Global and Shared Options:
- `m_ExportFormat` (`Pref<ExportFormat>`, key `"export.format"`, default `ExportFormat.Obj`): Dictates the active export handler and UI settings panel.
- `m_ExportRecursive` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.exportRecursive"`, default `false`): When enabled, mesh discovery uses `MeshSelection.deep.ToList()` to recurse down hierarchy trees; when disabled, only top-level selected meshes in `MeshSelection.topInternal` are exported.
- `m_ExportAsGroup` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.exportAsGroup"`, default `false`): When true, merges all selected mesh instances into a single output file. When false and multiple meshes are selected, prompts with `EditorUtility.SaveFolderPanel` and exports each mesh into its own named file. Displayed for `Obj` and `Ply` formats (hidden for `Asset`, `Prefab`, and `Stl`).

2. Format Specifications and Data Exported:
- Wavefront OBJ (`ExportFormat.Obj`):
  - Exported Data: Vertex coordinates (`v`), vertex color extensions (`v x y z r g b`), texture coordinates (`vt`), vertex normals (`vn`), polygonal face definitions (`f`), object identifier tags (`o`), grouping headers (`g`), material library links (`mtllib`), material binding declarations (`usemtl`), and copied image texture files.
  - Options:
    - `m_ObjExportRightHanded` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objExportRightHanded"`, default `true`): Inverts X axis coordinates and reverses vertex face winding for right-handed 3D software.
    - `m_ObjExportCopyTextures` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objExportCopyTextures"`, default `true`): Copies source material texture maps directly to the export folder. If false, writes absolute project paths.
    - `m_ObjApplyTransform` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objApplyTransform"`, default `false`): Transforms vertex coordinates and normals into world space prior to export. Automatically forced to true when `m_ExportAsGroup` is true.
    - `m_ObjExportVertexColors` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objExportVertexColors"`, default `false`): Writes RGB vertex colors directly after XYZ position values following MeshLab format.
    - `m_ObjTextureOffsetScale` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objTextureOffsetScale"`, default `false`): Writes `-o offset.x offset.y -s scale.x scale.y` parameters into MTL texture definitions.
    - `m_ObjQuads` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.objQuads"`, default `true`): Exports 4-sided faces as quads rather than triangulating.
- Stanford PLY (`ExportFormat.Ply`):
  - Exported Data: ASCII PLY 1.0 format with element vertex (`float32 x, y, z`, optional `float32 nx, ny, nz`, optional `uint8 red, green, blue, alpha`), element face (`list uint8 int32 vertex_index`), preserving quad or n-gon topology.
  - Options:
    - `m_PlyExportIsRightHanded` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.plyExportIsRightHanded"`, default `true`): Inverts X position, inverts X normal, and reverses face index ordering.
    - `m_PlyApplyTransform` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.plyApplyTransform"`, default `true`): Applies GameObject transform matrix to position (`TransformPoint`) and normal (`TransformDirection`).
    - `m_PlyQuads` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.plyQuads"`, default `true`): Converts quad faces to 4-vertex face elements.
    - `m_PlyNGons` (`Pref<bool>`, key `"export.plyNGons"`, default `false`): Writes arbitrary n-gon faces.
- STL (`ExportFormat.Stl`):
  - Exported Data: Triangle facet geometry with facet normals and outer loops (`facet normal ni nj nk`, `outer loop`, `vertex v1`, `vertex v2`, `vertex v3`). STL does not support UVs, colors, or materials.
  - Options:
    - `m_StlExportFormat` (`Pref<FileType>`, key `"export.stlExportFormat"`, default `FileType.Ascii`): Selects between `FileType.Ascii` and `FileType.Binary` (`UnityEngine.ProBuilder.Stl.FileType`). Invokes `pb_Stl_Exporter.Export(path, gameObjects, type)` wrapped with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`.
- Unity Mesh Asset and Prefab (`ExportFormat.Asset`, `ExportFormat.Prefab`):
  - Exported Data: Native serialized `UnityEngine.Mesh` (`.asset`) and optional `UnityEngine.GameObject` prefab (`.prefab`).
  - Options (`ExportAssetOptions` struct, key `"export.assetOptions"`):
    - `makePrefab` (`bool`, default `false`): When true, builds both a `.asset` mesh and a `.prefab` referencing the mesh asset.
    - `replaceOriginal` (`bool`, default `false`): When true, removes the `ProBuilderMesh` component from the scene object, binds the newly created asset to `MeshFilter.sharedMesh` and `MeshCollider.sharedMesh`, and links prefab instances via `PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAssetAndConnect`.

3. Post-Export Workflow:
- `PingExportedModel(string path)`: Checks if the output path resides inside `Application.dataPath`. If local to the project, calls `AssetDatabase.Refresh()`, converts the path to `Assets/...`, loads the asset via `AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<Object>`, and selects it in the project browser using `EditorGUIUtility.PingObject(o)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, exporting to OBJ and glTF is handled natively by `GLTFDocument` or custom exporters writing to `.obj`, `.ply`, and `.stl`. Exporting to `.tres` (ArrayMesh resource) or `.tscn` (PackedScene) mirrors `ExportFormat.Asset` and `ExportFormat.Prefab` using `ResourceSaver.save(mesh, path)` and `PackedScene.pack(node)`.

sections.heading: OBJ EXPORTER
sections.content:
The Wavefront OBJ exporter is implemented across `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ExportObj` and `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.ObjExporter`. It outputs 3D geometry into `.obj` model files alongside associated `.mtl` material libraries.

1. Coordinate System, Handedness, and Transform Rules:
- Unity operates in a left-handed coordinate system. When `options.handedness == ObjOptions.Handedness.Right` (the default setting), the exporter sets `float handedness = -1f` and `bool reverseWinding = true`.
- Vertex transformation: If `options.applyTransforms` is true or `options.handedness != ObjOptions.Handedness.Left`, every vertex position is transformed via `positions[i] = matrix.MultiplyPoint3x4(positions[i]); positions[i].x *= handedness;` and every normal is transformed via `normals[i] = matrix.MultiplyVector(normals[i]); normals[i].x *= handedness;`.
- Face winding: When `reverseWinding` is true, vertex indices are reversed during face emission. For quad increment `inc = 4`, offsets are `o0 = 3, o1 = 2, o2 = 1, o3 = 0`; for triangles (`inc = 3`), offsets are `o0 = 2, o1 = 1, o2 = 0`.

2. Vertex, Normal, UV, and Face Formatting:
- Indexing: Wavefront OBJ is 1-indexed. The exporter maintains cumulative offsets `positionOffset = 1`, `normalOffset = 1`, and `textureOffset = 1` across multiple models.
- Vertex positions (`AppendPositions`): Positions and optional vertex colors are deduplicated using `PositionColorKey` (a struct wrapping `IntVec3 position` and `IntVec4 color`). When `options.vertexColors` is false, outputs `v {x} {y} {z}`. When `options.vertexColors` is true, outputs `v {x} {y} {z} {r} {g} {b}` in invariant culture.
- Texture coordinates (`AppendArrayVec2`): Deduplicated using `IntVec2`. Formats entries as `vt {u} {v}`.
- Normals (`AppendArrayVec3`): Deduplicated using `IntVec3`. Formats entries as `vn {x} {y} {z}`.
- Faces: Formatted per submesh. For triangles: `f p0/t0/n0 p1/t1/n1 p2/t2/n2`. For quads: `f p0/t0/n0 p1/t1/n1 p2/t2/n2 p3/t3/n3`.

3. Material and MTL Library Generation (`WriteMtlContents`):
- Collects all unique `Material` references across all models and submeshes.
- Names are sanitized by replacing spaces with underscores (`material.name.Replace(" ", "_")`). Name collisions are resolved by appending incrementing numeric suffixes (`_1`, `_2`).
- Shader Texture Map Mapping: Iterates all texture properties on the material shader and maps them to standard MTL tags using `s_TextureMapKeys`:
  - `_MainTex` -> `map_Kd`
  - `_MetallicGlossMap` -> `map_Pm`
  - `_BumpMap` -> `bump`
  - `_ParallaxMap` -> `disp`
  - `_EmissionMap` -> `map_Ke`
  - `_DetailMask` -> `map_d`
- Color and Transparency:
  - URP/HDRP shaders (`_BaseColorMap` or `_BaseMap`): reads `_BaseColor` and outputs `Kd {r} {g} {b}` and `d {a}`.
  - Standard shaders (`_Color`): reads `mat.color` and outputs `Kd {r} {g} {b}` and `d {a}`.
  - Fallback: `Kd 1.0 1.0 1.0` and `d 1.0`.
- Texture Offset and Scale: When `options.textureOffsetScale` is true, outputs `-o {offset.x} {offset.y} -s {scale.x} {scale.y} {textureName}`.
- Texture copying: When `options.copyTextures` is true, outputs relative file names in the MTL file and copies actual texture files to the target directory via `File.Copy(path, dest)`. When false, writes full project paths.

4. Multi-Object Handling:
- Group Mode (`asGroup == true` or `models.Count() < 2`): Prompts `EditorUtility.SaveFilePanel("Export to Obj", "Assets", name, "obj")`. Emits a single `.obj` file containing all meshes. Writes an overall `o {name}` tag and separate `g {model.name}` tags for each model.
- Separate Files Mode (`asGroup == false` and `models.Count() >= 2`): Prompts `EditorUtility.SaveFolderPanel("Export to Obj", "Assets", "")`. Iterates each model and exports a distinct `{directory}/{model.name}.obj` and `{directory}/{model.name}.mtl`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, StandardMaterial3D properties map directly to MTL keys: `albedo_texture` to `map_Kd`, `albedo_color` to `Kd` and `d`, `roughness_texture` and `metallic_texture` to `map_Pm`, `normal_texture` to `bump`, `emission_texture` to `map_Ke`, and `uv1_scale`/`uv1_offset` to texture offset/scale parameters.

sections.heading: PLY EXPORTER
sections.content:
The Stanford PLY exporter is implemented in `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.PlyExporter` and `UnityEditor.ProBuilder.Actions.ExportPly`. It converts ProBuilder geometry into standard ASCII PLY 1.0 format.

1. ASCII File Structure and Header Generation (`WriteHeader`):
- PLY format output is strictly ASCII text (`format ascii 1.0`). ProBuilder does not implement binary PLY export; binary export is reserved for the STL format.
- Header structure:
  - `ply`
  - `format ascii 1.0`
  - `comment Exported by [ProBuilder](http://www.procore3d.com/probuilder)`
  - `comment <DateTime>`
  - `element vertex <vertexCount>`
  - `property float32 x`
  - `property float32 y`
  - `property float32 z`
  - Conditional normal properties: `property float32 nx`, `property float32 ny`, `property float32 nz` (emitted if normals are present).
  - Conditional color properties: `property uint8 red`, `property uint8 green`, `property uint8 blue`, `property uint8 alpha` (emitted if colors are present).
  - `element face <faceCount>`
  - `property list uint8 int32 vertex_index`
  - `end_header`

2. Vertex Color Support:
- Vertex colors are read from each mesh using `x.GetColors()`.
- Colors are converted from floating-point `Color` values (0.0 to 1.0) to 8-bit unsigned integers (0 to 255) using `System.Math.Min(System.Math.Max(0, (int)(color * 255)), 255)` for each of `r`, `g`, `b`, and `a` channels.

3. Coordinate Handedness and Transforms:
- Coordinate transformation: When `options.applyTransforms` is true, positions are transformed with `trs.TransformPoint(positions[i])` and normals with `trs.TransformDirection(normals[i])`.
- Right-handed conversion: When `options.isRightHanded` is true (the default), `flipHandedness` is set. The X component of position is negated (`-positions[i].x`), the X component of normal is negated (`-normals[i].x`), and face vertex indices are emitted in reverse order (`faces[i][faceLength - n - 1]`).

4. Face Index Handling (Triangles, Quads, N-gons):
- When `options.ngons` is true, face indices are emitted directly or converted to quads if `options.quads && face.IsQuad()`.
- When `options.ngons` is false, each face is converted to quads via `face.ToQuad()` if `options.quads && face.IsQuad()`, or decomposed into triangle triplets: `face.indexesInternal[i + 0]`, `face.indexesInternal[i + 1]`, `face.indexesInternal[i + 2]`.
- Vertex offsets (`vertexOffset`) accumulate across models so multiple combined meshes reference correct continuous indices.

5. Multi-Object File Handling (`ExportPly.ExportWithFileDialog`):
- When `asGroup == true` or selected meshes count is less than 2, prompts `EditorUtility.SaveFilePanel("Export as PLY", "Assets", name, "ply")` and writes a single combined `.ply` file.
- When `asGroup == false` and multiple meshes exist, prompts `EditorUtility.SaveFolderPanel("Export to PLY", "Assets", "")` and writes individual `{directory}/{model.name}.ply` files.
sections.godot_notes: Godot does not include a built-in PLY exporter in core, but PLY import is supported via plugins. In a Godot reimplementation, this ASCII generation translates directly into Godot `FileAccess` string writing or binary stream writing.

sections.heading: MESH IMPORTER
sections.content:
The conversion of external or standard Unity meshes into ProBuilder editable format is handled by `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.MeshOperations.MeshImporter` and configured by `MeshImportSettings`.

1. Import Configuration (`MeshImportSettings`):
- `quads` (`bool m_Quads`, default `true`): Dictates whether triangular face pairs are evaluated and merged into quad polygons.
- `smoothing` (`bool m_Smoothing`, default `true`): Dictates whether smoothing groups are computed and assigned based on vertex normals.
- `smoothingAngle` (`float m_SmoothingThreshold`, default `1f`): Angular tolerance threshold in degrees for grouping adjacent face normals.

2. Topology Ingestion and Vertex Splitting Algorithm:
- The importer accepts either a `GameObject` (extracting `MeshFilter.sharedMesh` and `MeshRenderer.sharedMaterials`) or explicit `(Mesh sourceMesh, Material[] sourceMaterials, ProBuilderMesh destination)` arguments.
- Topology Verification: Iterates submeshes in `m_SourceMesh`. If any submesh has topology other than `MeshTopology.Triangles` or `MeshTopology.Quads`, throws a `NotSupportedException`.
- Vertex Unsharing Pipeline: ProBuilder geometry representation requires discrete vertices per face before welding. The importer reads `sourceVertices = m_SourceMesh.GetVertices()` and constructs unshared vertex buffers:
  - For Triangles: Iterates index triplets `(tri, tri+1, tri+2)`. Creates a new `Face` with indices `[vertexIndex, vertexIndex+1, vertexIndex+2]`, submesh index clamped to `[0, materialCount - 1]`, `AutoUnwrapSettings.tile`, `Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone`, and `manualUV = true`. Adds 3 distinct `Vertex` instances to `splitVertices`. Increments `vertexIndex += 3`.
  - For Quads: Iterates index quartets `(quad, quad+1, quad+2, quad+3)`. Creates a new `Face` with 6 triangle indices `[vertexIndex, vertexIndex+1, vertexIndex+2, vertexIndex+2, vertexIndex+3, vertexIndex+0]`, clamped submesh index, `AutoUnwrapSettings.tile`, `Smoothing.smoothingGroupNone`, and `manualUV = true`. Adds 4 distinct `Vertex` instances to `splitVertices`. Increments `vertexIndex += 4`.

3. Destination Mesh Assignment and Vertex Sharing Heuristics:
- Resets destination state: calls `m_Destination.Clear()`, `m_Destination.SetVertices(m_Vertices)`, `m_Destination.faces = faces`.
- Vertex Sharing: Computes coincident vertex grouping via `m_Destination.sharedVertices = SharedVertex.GetSharedVerticesWithPositions(m_Destination.positionsInternal)`. This groups vertices that occupy identical spatial coordinates into shared index clusters, establishing edge and vertex connectivity for editing operations.
- Shared Textures: Initializes `m_Destination.sharedTextures = new SharedVertex[0]`.

4. Post-Import Processing:
- Quad Reconstruction: If `importSettings.quads` is enabled, calls `m_Destination.ToQuads(m_Destination.facesInternal, !importSettings.smoothing)`. If smoothing is disabled, quad conversion avoids merging faces across hard normal boundaries.
- Smoothing Group Assignment: If `importSettings.smoothing` is enabled, calls `Smoothing.ApplySmoothingGroups(m_Destination, m_Destination.facesInternal, importSettings.smoothingAngle, m_Vertices.Select(x => x.normal).ToArray())`.
- Coincident Vertex Welding: After smoothing group calculation, calls `MergeElements.CollapseCoincidentVertices(m_Destination, m_Destination.facesInternal)` to weld duplicate vertices created during quad merging.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, converting an `ArrayMesh` or `ImporterMesh` into a custom ProBuilder mesh requires extracting surface arrays (`Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX`, `Mesh.ARRAY_NORMAL`, `Mesh.ARRAY_TEX_UV`, `Mesh.ARRAY_INDEX`), unindexing triangles into distinct vertices, constructing `Face` records with material indices, and building a spatial hash to generate shared vertex tables.

sections.heading: MATERIAL EDITOR
sections.content:
The Material Editor is an editor utility window (`UnityEditor.ProBuilder.MaterialEditor` inheriting from `ConfigurableWindow`) that manages material assignment, palette presets, and quick material picking across ProBuilder meshes.

1. Quick Material Picker:
- Backing State: `m_QueuedMaterial` (`Pref<Material>`, key `"materialEditor.quickMaterial"`, scope `SettingsScope.User`, default `null`).
- Preview Display: Renders a 64x64 GUI box displaying the preview texture retrieved via `EditorMaterialUtility.GetPreviewTexture(m_QueuedMaterial.value)`. `GetPreviewTexture` inspects shader properties on the material: checks for `_MainTex` or `Albedo` textures first, falling back to any available `Texture2D`. If no texture exists, renders a box with `"None\n(Texture)"`.
- Match Selection: When `MeshSelection.selectedFaceCount > 0`, the "Match Selection" button is enabled. Clicking it invokes `m_QueuedMaterial.SetValue(EditorMaterialUtility.GetActiveSelection())`. `EditorMaterialUtility.GetActiveSelection()` queries `MeshSelection.activeMesh` and `MeshSelection.activeFace`: returns `sharedMaterials[face.submeshIndex]` or the mesh renderer's `sharedMaterial`.
- Quick Material Application: Executed via "Apply" button, menu item `"Tools/ProBuilder/Materials/Apply Quick Material"`, or scene shortcut `Shift + Control + Mouse2` registered through `MaterialShortcutContext` with Unity's `ShortcutManager`.

2. Material Palette UI and Storage (`MaterialPalette`):
- ScriptableObject Model: `MaterialPalette` stores `public Material[] array` (default 10 elements). Contains implicit conversion `public static implicit operator Material[](MaterialPalette materialArray)`.
- Default initialization: `SetDefaultValues()` initializes an array of 10 elements with slot 0 set to `BuiltinMaterials.defaultMaterial` and slots 1–9 set to null.
- Palette Selection: A dropdown popup lists all available palettes discovered in the project via `FileUtility.FindAndLoadAssets<MaterialPalette>()`, along with a trailing entry `"New Material Palette..."`.
- Saving and Creating: Creating a new palette generates a unique asset at `Assets/Material Palette.asset` via `FileUtility.LoadRequired<MaterialPalette>(path)`. Any modification immediately calls `SaveUserMaterials(materials)` which updates `s_CurrentPalette.array`, marks dirty with `EditorUtility.SetDirty(s_CurrentPalette)`, and saves via `AssetDatabase.SaveAssets()`.
- Dynamic Wells Expansion: Slots 0 through 9 have preset buttons `Apply 0` to `Apply 9` (mapped to menu shortcuts `Alt + 1` through `Alt + 0`). When additional slots are added beyond 10, a separator is rendered (`UI.EditorGUIUtility.DrawSeparator(1)`). Each extra slot displays a split mini-button: an `Apply` button (width 44) and a red delete square (width 14). Clicking "Add" allocates an array of size `materials.Length + 1` and persists it.

3. Material Application Algorithm (`ApplyMaterial`):
- Undo Registration: Calls `UndoUtility.RecordComponents<MeshRenderer, ProBuilderMesh>(selection, "Set Material")`.
- Face vs Object Mode: Evaluates `bool applyPerFace = ProBuilderEditor.instance != null && ProBuilderEditor.selectMode.ContainsFlag(SelectMode.Face) && mesh.faceCount > 0;`.
- Assignment: Calls `mesh.SetMaterial(applyPerFace ? mesh.GetSelectedFaces() : mesh.facesInternal, mat)`.
- Cleanup and Optimization: Calls `InternalMeshUtility.FilterUnusedSubmeshIndexes(mesh)` to prune orphaned submesh slots, followed by `mesh.Rebuild()` and `mesh.Optimize()`.
- Feedback: Displays editor notification `EditorUtility.ShowNotification("Set Material\n" + mat.name)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, a Material Palette dock can be implemented as an `EditorPlugin` dock with a custom `Resource` (`MaterialPaletteResource`) holding an `Array[Material]`. Applying materials modifies surface material overrides on `MeshInstance3D` or individual face submesh indices in the custom mesh resource.

sections.heading: BUILTIN MATERIALS
sections.content:
ProBuilder provides a centralized catalog of built-in materials, shaders, and loading mechanisms in `UnityEngine.ProBuilder.BuiltinMaterials`.

1. Default Materials and Instantiation:
- `defaultMaterial` (`Material`): Loads `Resources.Load("Materials/ProBuilderDefault", typeof(Material))` and sets its shader to `Shader.Find("ProBuilder6/Standard Vertex Color")`. If the asset is missing or unsupported on the current graphics device, falls back to `GetLegacyDiffuse()`.
- `GetLegacyDiffuse()`: Queries the engine default material using reflection (`typeof(Material).GetMethod("GetDefaultMaterial", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static)`). If reflection returns null, creates a temporary primitive `GameObject.CreatePrimitive(PrimitiveType.Cube)` to extract `MeshRenderer.sharedMaterial`, immediately destroying the cube via `Object.DestroyImmediate(go)`.
- `ShapePreviewMaterial`: Instantiated dynamically via `new Material(defaultMaterial.shader)` with `HideFlags.HideAndDontSave`. Sets `mainTexture = Resources.Load("Textures/GridBox_Default")` and tint color `_Color` to `previewColor = new Color(0.5f, 0.9f, 1f, 0.56f)`.

2. Selection and Interaction Materials:
- Selection Picker Materials: Loaded from `Resources` with fallbacks:
  - `facePickerMaterial`: `Resources.Load<Material>("com.unity.probuilder/Materials/FacePicker")` (or `FacePickerURP` under `#if PB_URP_MODE`). Fallback: `new Material(Shader.Find(k_FacePickerShader))`.
  - `vertexPickerMaterial`: `Resources.Load<Material>("com.unity.probuilder/Materials/VertexPicker")` (or `VertexPickerURP`). Fallback: `new Material(Shader.Find(k_VertexPickerShader))`.
  - `edgePickerMaterial`: `Resources.Load<Material>("com.unity.probuilder/Materials/EdgePicker")` (or `EdgePickerURP`). Fallback: `new Material(Shader.Find(k_EdgePickerShader))`.
- Entity Materials:
  - `triggerMaterial`: Loaded from `Resources.Load("Materials/Trigger", typeof(Material))`.
  - `colliderMaterial`: Loaded from `Resources.Load("Materials/Collider", typeof(Material))`.

3. Shaders and Device Capability Detection:
- Built-in Shader Names:
  - `faceShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/FaceHighlight"`
  - `lineShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboard"` (geometry shader)
  - `lineShaderMetal` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/LineBillboardMetal"`
  - `pointShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/PointBillboard"` (geometry shader)
  - `wireShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/FaceHighlight"` (fallback when geometry shaders are unsupported)
  - `dotShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/VertexShader"` (fallback when geometry shaders are unsupported)
  - `selectionPickerShader` = `"Hidden/ProBuilder/SelectionPicker"` (or `SelectionPickerURP`)
- Geometry Shader Check (`geometryShadersSupported`): Checks `Shader.Find(lineShader)` and inspects `isSupported`. If false, drawing routines switch from billboard geometry shaders to CPU billboard meshes (`lineShaderMetal` / `wireShader` / `dotShader`).

4. Lazy Initialization and Reset Mechanics:
- `Init()` executes lazily upon initial property access, setting `s_IsInitialized = true`, evaluating geometry shader support, and caching picking shaders and materials.
- In the Unity Editor, `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.BeforeSceneLoad)]` executes `ResetStaticsOnLoad()`, clearing `s_DefaultMaterial`, `s_UnityDefaultDiffuse`, `s_ShapePreviewMaterial`, and re-invoking `Init()`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, default and preview materials can be defined as `StandardMaterial3D` resources loaded from `res://addons/probuilder/materials/`. Picking and wireframe overlays use custom `ShaderMaterial` with shaders compiled for Godot's Vulkan/OpenGL renderers without requiring geometry shaders.

cross_references.relationship: ProBuilderMesh core data structures and arrays (positionsInternal, facesInternal, sharedVertices) manipulated by exporters and MeshImporter.
Face, Edge, and SharedVertex data models used by MeshImporter, PlyExporter, and MaterialEditor.
MergeElements.CollapseCoincidentVertices used by MeshImporter to weld coincident vertices after quad conversion.
AutoUnwrapSettings.tile applied to faces during external mesh conversion in MeshImporter.
Shaders, wireframes, and selection picker materials defined in BuiltinMaterials.
MenuAction base class, TooltipContent, and ToolbarGroup used by Export, ExportObj, ExportPly, ExportStl, and ExportAsset.
StripProBuilderScripts.DestroyProBuilderMeshAndDependencies used by ExportAsset when replaceOriginal is true.
Smoothing.ApplySmoothingGroups used by MeshImporter to calculate smoothing groups from surface normal angles.
